confirmed.title: Pending pass: the worker cursor advances at most one worker per page, so decode pending pages land outside their KV head's block
confirmed.detail:
The page-centre walk moves the cursor with `if (worker_cumsum[worker] < page_center && worker + 1 < worker_cumsum.size()) ++worker;` (one step per page). The old one-walk code had the same `if`, but the many ready pages of every head carried the cursor to the head's block before its pending pages came. In the new pending pass the walk restarts at worker 0 with only the pending pages, and in decode there are few of them (one page per user that writes KV this forward, shared by all KV heads). When a head has fewer pending pages than workers, the cursor cannot reach the head's block: head k's pending pages land on the workers right after head k-1's pending pages, not on the workers that hold head k's ready pages.

Simulated with the walk as written (scratchpad script walk.py, total = pages / kv_heads summed over heads, equal worker speeds):
- 8 users, prompt 1024 (128 ready pages, 8 pending pages per head), 4 KV heads, 40 workers (10 per head): head 1's pending pages go to workers 8-15 (block 10-19), head 3's to workers 24-31 (block 30-39). Old code: workers 18-19 and 38-39.
- 1 user, 8 KV heads, 32 workers (4 per head): head k's single pending page lands on worker k+1, i.e. all 8 pending pages on workers 1-8 (blocks of heads 0 and 1). Old code: the last worker of each block (3, 7, ..., 31).

Why it matters: every page is still assigned exactly once and the ready pass still runs before the K/V wait (run_attention_job runs ready_kv_plan, waits, then pending_kv_plan, self_attention.hpp:841-853), so results stay correct. But the plan is not what the comment at model.hpp:2896 claims ("its pending pages spread over the same workers as its ready pages"): a worker outside head k's block now holds a head-k pending section, so (Step 5, model.hpp:2438-2446) it joins one more KV head (extra kv_heads_to_join entry, extra scratchpad fold per token for that head), and head k's join waits for a worker that first runs another head's ready sections. In the 1-user case, workers 1-8 each carry one pending page while 24 workers carry none, and the join of head 7 depends on worker 8. This contradicts the design intent "decode neutral" and the comment; it also loses the L2 locality the join scheme relies on (Note [Attention join parallelism scheme]).
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed by reading the code and re-running the walk. In place_pages (/home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-glimmer-planner/h/tron/models/model.hpp:2961-2967) the cursor advance is a single `if`, so it moves at most one worker per page. The parent commit 5061623a34 had the same `if`, but there the ready pages of each head carried the cursor into the head's block before its pending pages were placed. In the new weighted path, place_pages({1}) restarts at worker 0 with prior_work counting only pending_kv_plan, so in decode (few pending pages per head) the cursor lags behind the head's block. Simulation of the walk as written (equal speeds, unit work, scratchpad script /tmp/claude-0/-home-jhan-workspace-intel-AMX-muse-glimmer/2286d13f-0c9b-4afd-a521-f1f97342a0e9/scratchpad/walk.py) reproduces both cases in the finding: 8 pending pages/head, 4 heads, 40 workers: head 1 pending on workers 8-15 (its ready block is 10-19), head 3 on 24-31 (block 30-39); old one-walk code put them on 19 and 39. 1 pending page/head, 8 heads, 32 workers: head k's page on worker k+1 (workers 1-8, all inside the blocks of heads 0-1); old code: 3, 7, ..., 31. With the `while` form, every head's pending pages stay inside its block (8u: [10,11,13,14,15,16,18,19] for head 1; 1u: 1, 5, 9, ..., 29). Why it matters: Step 5 (model.hpp:2438-2446) inserts section.kv_head into kv_heads_to_join[worker] and join_workers[kv_head] for every section of both passes, so a worker outside head k's block now joins head k too (one more scratchpad fold per token for that head, two heads to join on that worker), and the L2-locality assumption of Note [Attention join parallelism scheme] (self_attention.hpp:1259-1262, 'only those kv heads that this same thread has worked on before') is broken for every pending page in decode. Results stay correct (each page assigned once; ready sections run, then the K/V wait, then pending sections, self_attention.hpp:841-853), but the comment at model.hpp:2894-2897 claims an alignment the code does not deliver, and the commit's stated intent 'decode neutral' is not met by construction. The size of the decode effect is unmeasured (Insufficient data: a decode TPS cell with and without the fix would resolve it), but the misplacement itself is deterministic and is in the common decode shape, so this is a real defect, not a taste nit.

confirmed.title: Weighted path drops zero-work ready pages (hardware-attention layers) instead of planning them as zero-work sections
confirmed.detail: `place_pages` returns before assigning any page when the pass total is 0: `if (total_work == 0) return 0;` with the comment "No SW pages in this pass". In a hardware-attention layer during decode the ready pages are present but hardware-covered, so their work is 0 while the pending pages (the new tokens, scored in software) have work. The old code returned only when the total over BOTH passes was 0; otherwise it walked every page, so each ready page became part of a zero-work section (kv_plan::assign_page keeps zero-work runs as their own sections, common.hpp:987-989; the fixture comment at t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3110 says these exist "for join-worker accounting"). Under TRON_PLAN_WEIGHTED_DISABLE=1 (`place_pages({0, 1})`) the old behaviour is kept, so the default and the kill-switch plans differ in a hardware-attention layer: with the weights on, no zero-work ready sections, fewer n_sections, and join_workers[kv_head] built from the pending sections only (Step 5, model.hpp:2438-2446). Consequence: a different join-worker set per head (in the old walk the zero-work pages of a head all landed on the cursor's worker, which was then also a join worker for that head) and the per-worker run_sections no longer visits those pages (the visit was cheap: dismiss_workless_ranges in apply_page_range). This is a plan change for FPGA-attention models that the commit message does not state and the kill switch does not reproduce, so an A/B between the two switch states on such a model measures more than the weights and the two walks.
confirmed.fix: Keep the new behaviour on purpose and say so: (a) in the commit message and Note [Path-weighted attention plan] add one sentence: "When a pass has no software work (the ready pass of a hardware-attention layer), its pages are not planned; zero-work ready sections no longer exist, and join_workers comes from the productive sections. TRON_PLAN_WEIGHTED_DISABLE=1 keeps the old zero-work sections." (b) Replace the comment at model.hpp:2937-2938 ("No SW pages in this pass: nothing to place. Returning here avoids a div-by-zero") with one that states the plan effect, not only the div-by-zero. (c) Extend the new test case: call finish_sw_plan after estimate(use_hw=true, amx_on=true) with page_work[0] forced to zero work (or a fixture whose ready ranges are not sw_required) and CHECK that every ready_kv_plan[worker] is empty, that n_sections[kv_head] equals the number of pending sections, and that join_workers would be non-empty from pending sections alone. If instead the old accounting is wanted, return early only when both passes total 0 and, in a zero-total pass, assign each head's pages to the current cursor worker without the division (page_center = worker_cumsum[worker]), which reproduces the old zero-work sections; then the test checks that a zero-work ready section exists per head on a worker that also holds that head's first pending section.
confirmed.verdict: Verified in the worktree. (1) place_pages returns before assigning any page when its pass total is 0 [model.hpp:2939]; the old code and the kill-switch path (place_pages({0,1})) return only when ready+pending is 0 and otherwise walk every page, so zero-work pages become zero-work sections (assign_page keeps zero-work runs as their own sections, common.hpp:983-989). (2) The ready-total-0 / pending-total>0 case is the normal state of every hardware-attention layer: select_relevant_pages keeps a page when any item has range.visible() [model.hpp:2504-2510], while estimate_work under use_hw credits work only when range.sw_required() [model.hpp:2599], so hardware-covered ready pages are in batch_page_ixs[0] with work() 0 and the pending pages (software-scored under hardware attention, per the estimate_work comment at 2555-2557) carry the work. (3) Consequences are as stated: n_sections[kv_head] counts only pending sections, join_workers[kv_head] is built from pending sections only (Step 5, 2438-2446), and run_sections no longer runs the zero-work ready sections (apply_page_range dismissed them cheaply via dismiss_workless_ranges, self_attention.hpp:1541-1550). In the old walk the zero-work ready pages of head k land on the cursor worker left by head k-1; when head k's first pending page advances the cursor, that worker is a join worker for head k with no productive partial. So the default plan on FPGA-attention models differs from the kill-switch plan in a third way the commit message does not list ("two passes" + weights only), and a same-binary A/B on such a model measures it too. No correctness defect: joins fold invalid scratchpads as identity, Step 6 covers an empty join set, sections_left stays consistent with n_sections, and the new test runs finish_sw_plan only with use_hw=false (t_llama_unit.cpp:3616-3626), so nothing pins which behaviour is intended. Severity low; the change is probably neutral or slightly favourable (fewer pointless sections, join set = productive workers), but it is unstated and untested.

confirmed.title: New plan test uses a shape where the cursor never has to move more than one worker per page, so it cannot detect finding 1
confirmed.detail: The test places 6 ready + 2 pending pages per head on 4 workers (2 per head) and checks `pending_workers == block`. With 2 pending pages per head and 2 workers per head, the one-step-per-page cursor advance happens to reach every worker (page p6 of head 1 moves the cursor from worker 1 to 2, p7 from 2 to 3). The decode shape that production runs (one pending page per user, several workers per head) is not covered, and that is exactly where the pending pass misplaces pages (plan-correctness-1). The test therefore passes today while the comment it is meant to verify ("pending pages of a KV head must land on the same workers as its ready pages", line 3614-3616) is false for decode.
confirmed.fix: In t_llama_unit.cpp after the 4-worker check (line ~3632), add a second finish_sw_plan call on fresh plans with n_workers = 8 (worker_cumsum = {0.125, 0.25, ..., 1.0}, workers_per_kv_head = 4) and the same 6 ready + 2 pending pages per head. Assert containment, not equality: for every kv_head, every worker holding a pending section of that head is in [kv_head * 4, kv_head * 4 + 4). With the current `if` at model.hpp:2963 head 1's pending pages land on workers 2 and 3 (head 0's block) and the check fails; after changing the `if` to `while (worker_cumsum[worker] < page_center && worker + 1 < worker_cumsum.size())` (adding prior_work(worker) on each step) they land on workers 4 and 6 and the check passes. Optionally also keep a one-pending-page variant (num_pages = 7, n_ready_pages = 6) to match the decode shape directly; the 8-worker variant already fails with the `if`.
confirmed.verdict: Verified by reading finish_sw_plan (model.hpp:2928-2983) and the test (t_llama_unit.cpp:3484-3632) and walking the pending pass by hand with the test's real numbers. Test shape: n_q = 64, n_kv_heads = 2, visits = 128, page 6 work = 1 x 128 = 128, page 7 (diagonal) work = 3 x 128 = 384, pending total_work = 512, per-head page work 64 and 192, worker_cumsum = {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}. Page centres in walk order: head 0 p6 = 0.0625 (stays on worker 0), head 0 p7 = 0.3125 (> 0.25, cursor to 1), head 1 p6 = 0.5625 (> 0.5, cursor to 2), head 1 p7 = 0.8125 (> 0.75, cursor to 3). Every page crosses exactly one worker boundary, so the single-step `if` at model.hpp:2963 lands each head's pending pages on exactly its block {0,1} / {2,3} and both CHECKs at lines 3627-3628 pass. The test therefore cannot distinguish the `if` from a `while`. With 8 equal workers (cumsum (w+1)/8) and the same pages, the `if` gives head 0 p6 -> worker 0, head 0 p7 -> worker 1 (centre 0.3125 needs worker 2), head 1 p6 -> worker 2 (centre 0.5625 needs worker 4, block {4..7}), head 1 p7 -> worker 3: head 1's pending pages both sit in head 0's block, contradicting the comment at test lines 3614-3616 and model.hpp:2895-2897. The same happens in the production decode shape (one pending page per user, several workers per head): head k's pending page lands on worker k+1. The `if` predates the commit but was harmless in the one-walk regime (many pages per worker); the new separate pending pass with fewer pages than workers is the regime where it misplaces pages, and this test is the only one that exercises that pass. Not a taste point: the test's stated purpose (pending pages on the ready workers of the head) is not checked by its shape.

confirmed.title: New planner test binds dense_page / partial_page to elements of empty vectors and keeps them across reallocations
confirmed.detail: Lines 3570-3571 bind `const work_estimate_t& dense_page = page_work[1][0]` and `partial_page = page_work[1][1]` before the first `estimate(...)` call (line 3576). At that point `page_work[1]` is a default-constructed empty vector, so operator[] forms a reference to address null (with -D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS it aborts at the binding). The `estimate` lambda (lines 3554-3563) then does `page_work = {}` (move-assign from an empty array frees each vector's buffer) and `estimate_work` resizes into a new allocation, so even a reference taken after one call dangles across the next call. First dereference is line 3589 (`partial_page.k_dot_products`), then 3590-3594, 3601-3604, 3609-3611. The test therefore crashes the whole t_llama_unit run (SIGSEGV or abort) instead of checking the weights; tests.sh in exec/glimpl-20261017 runs t_llama_unit, and no run log exists in that directory, so there is no evidence the test ever passed.
confirmed.fix:
In t/t_llama_unit.cpp replace lines 3570-3571 with accessors that read the element after each estimate call:
  auto dense_page = [&]() -> const work_estimate_t& { return page_work[1][0]; };    // page 6
  auto partial_page = [&]() -> const work_estimate_t& { return page_work[1][1]; };  // page 7
and change every later use to `dense_page()` / `partial_page()` (lines 3589-3596, 3601-3604, 3610-3611). Alternatively keep plain references but take them inside each block right after its `estimate(...)` call (`const work_estimate_t& dense_page = page_work[1][0];` after 3576, again after 3600 and 3608) with distinct scopes. Then build and run `gen/t_llama_unit "attention plan weights pages by path and spreads pending pages"` (ideally also with -D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS) at the head and keep the log under exec/glimpl-20261017/.
confirmed.verdict: Verified in the worktree. t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3570-3571 bind `const work_estimate_t& dense_page = page_work[1][0]` and `partial_page = page_work[1][1]` while `page_work` (declared at 3551, never filled before) holds default-constructed empty vectors. operator[] on an empty std::vector is undefined; with libstdc++ the reference is formed at `_M_start + 0` = address null, and with -D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS the binding itself aborts. The `estimate` lambda (3554-3563) then does `page_work = {}` and calls `state.estimate_work`, which resizes the vectors (model.hpp:2551 `page_work[pending].resize(page_ixs.size())`) into a fresh allocation, so a reference taken before or between calls never points at the populated element. The references are dereferenced at 3589-3596, 3601-3604 and 3610-3611, so the test either aborts or reads null, which takes down the whole t_llama_unit binary rather than one CHECK. No run evidence exists: exec/glimpl-20261017 holds only scripts (build.sh, tests.sh, chain.sh, campaign.sh, launch.sh, gen_compare.py, planner.diff) and the worktree has no gen/t_llama_unit, so nothing shows the test passed. The defect is real, not taste.

confirmed.title: pass_amx adds a use_hw && pending term that the kernel dispatch does not have
confirmed.detail: `const bool pass_amx = amx_on && !(use_hw && pending);` forces every pending-pass visit under hardware attention to the AVX cost (3 units) regardless of the predicate. The kernel's dispatch has no such term: run_sections (self_attention.hpp:1563-1565) sets `amx_on = eligible && available()` with no pending or uses_hw check, and apply_page_tok (self_attention.hpp:1886-1889) takes the AMX path on `amx_q_packed != nullptr && is_dense_amx_page(...)` alone. So the planner and the kernel can disagree only in one direction: if a pending page under HW ever satisfies the predicate (a whole page whose last token is below the first token's range tok_hi, sw_required for the query), the kernel runs it on AMX at cost 1 while the plan charges 3, which is the same kind of imbalance this commit is meant to remove; if that never happens, the term is dead code. The justification is a measurement (0 AMX visits in the pending pass of the 2026-10-16 FPGA cells), not a dispatch rule, and the Note at common.hpp:687-689 ('classifies every visit with the kernel's own dense predicate') contradicts it. Whether the term ever fires in production is Insufficient data (would need attention path stats per pass on an FPGA-attention model with chunked prefill).
confirmed.fix: At /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-glimmer-planner/h/tron/models/model.hpp:2553-2556 drop the override so the planner follows the dispatch rule the kernel uses: `const bool pass_amx = amx_on;` (and delete the three-line comment about the pending pass measurement, or keep it as an observation: "Measured 2026-10-16 with hardware attention: no pending-pass visit passed the predicate."). Then update the test hunk in t/t_llama_unit.cpp that asserts the pending whole page counts as AVX under use_hw=true (the `estimate(/*use_hw=*/true, /*amx_on=*/true)` block): with the term gone that page is dense, so change the expectations to `dense_page.amx_dense_visits == visits` and `avx_full_visits == 0`, or build the pending page from per-token ranges the way the range builder does (one range per query token) so it is AVX by the predicate itself. The Note at common.hpp:687-689 then stays true without edits. If the author instead wants to keep the override, the gate must be added to the kernel too (null amx_q_packed for pending sections under hardware attention in run_sections) and Note [AMX attention dispatch] and Note [Path-weighted attention plan] must both state the rule; keeping it on one side only is the defect.
confirmed.verdict: Verified by reading the worktree. The planner's gate is at model.hpp:2556 (not 2558): `const bool pass_amx = amx_on && !(use_hw && pending);`. The kernel has no such term: run_sections sets `amx_on = amx_eligible && amx_attn_h128g4::available()` (self_attention.hpp:1563-1565) and apply_page_tok takes the AMX path on `amx_q_packed != nullptr && is_dense_amx_page(...)` alone (self_attention.hpp:1888-1890), with `query_visible = range_hint->sw_required(job_ix)` under hardware attention (1876-1877), which is the same input the planner passes as `contributes_to_sw` (model.hpp:2599). So the planner's predicate call already mirrors the kernel's rule exactly, and the extra term can only make the two sides disagree, never agree better. The commit's own test proves the divergence is reachable at the predicate level: with use_hw=true the pending whole page is dense per the predicate (the same page is counted amx_dense_visits == visits in the ready slot) and only the term forces it to AVX. Whether that case occurs in production is Insufficient data (the commit cites 0 AMX pending visits in the 2026-10-16 FPGA cells; the range builder in ranged_mask.cpp puts a boundary at every query token, so prefill-chunk pending pages are never dense, but a decode step that fills a page whose earlier tokens are still in one SW range would be). Impact is therefore bounded: either the term is dead code, or it mis-weights a visit 3:1 in the direction the commit set out to remove. The concrete defect that stands regardless is the comment-vs-code contradiction: Note [Path-weighted attention plan] (common.hpp:687-689) says estimate_work "classifies every visit with the kernel's own dense predicate (is_dense_amx_page)", and the commit message says the same, while the code adds a measurement-derived override. Severity: low rather than medium.

confirmed.title: pass_amx rule for the pending pass under hardware attention is justified by a measurement, not by the kernel's gate
confirmed.detail: Line 2556 'const bool pass_amx = amx_on && !(use_hw && pending);' with the comment (2553-2555) 'With hardware attention the pending pass measured no AMX visit in any cell (attention path stats, 2026-10-16), so its pages count as AVX.' The commit's stated design is that the planner predicts the path 'with the kernel's own dense predicate' (common.hpp Note, model.hpp:2614-2617). This line adds a second rule that the kernel does not have: apply_page_tok (self_attention.hpp:1877-1899) decides per (query, page) from amx_q_packed != nullptr and is_dense_amx_page alone, with no 'pending' or 'uses_hw' input; amx_on in run_sections (self_attention.hpp:1562-1565) also ignores the pass. The planner already mirrors the kernel's visibility for HW models at model.hpp:2599-2600 (use_hw ? sw_required : visible), so if the mechanism is 'whole pending pages are never sw_required under FPGA attention', the predicate alone already returns false and line 2556 is dead; if the mechanism is something else (for example page.count() at kernel time differs from planning time), the comment does not name it. A measurement on one date and one model set is the Wade 'guarantee wider than the code' pattern: a future FPGA-attention model whose pending whole pages do take AMX (any model where sw_required covers a whole pending page) would be charged 3x on those pages with no test to catch it, and nothing in the code says which condition would make the rule wrong.
confirmed.fix: Take option (a). In model.hpp:2553-2556 replace `const bool pass_amx = amx_on && !(use_hw && pending);` with `const bool pass_amx = amx_on;` and delete the measurement sentence, so the planner's prediction is exactly the kernel's gate (amx_on plus is_dense_amx_page with contributes_to_sw, which already mirrors run_visible_in_software via use_hw ? sw_required : visible). In t_llama_unit.cpp:3604-3611 change the use_hw=true block: either (i) keep the fixture and assert what the predicate gives there (page_work[0][n_ready_pages-1].amx_dense_visits == visits and dense_page.amx_dense_visits == visits, with a comment that under hardware attention the pending page counts dense when its tokens are software-required and lie in one range, the same gate as apply_page_tok), or (ii) make the fixture production-like by giving page 6 one query token per KV token (one mask range per token, as build_edge_ranges emits) and assert that page 6 is then AVX full under both use_hw values. (ii) also pins the real reason prefill pending pages are never dense. If the 2026-10-16 measurement is to be kept as context, move it to the commit message or PR body, not to a code comment presented as the rule's cause.
confirmed.verdict: Verified by reading the worktree. (1) The kernel's AMX gate has no pass or hardware input: apply_page_tok (self_attention.hpp:1888-1890) takes the AMX path from amx_q_packed != nullptr and is_dense_amx_page alone, and run_sections passes `pending` only to the plan lookup and the stats pass label (1190, 1703). So the planner's extra term `!(use_hw && pending)` (model.hpp:2556) is a rule the kernel does not apply, while the Note [Path-weighted attention plan] (common.hpp:687-688) and the estimate_work comment (model.hpp:2614-2617) say the planner uses "the kernel's own dense predicate". That is a comment-contradicts-code defect. (2) The term is not dead: the test fixture (t_llama_unit.cpp:3525-3537) marks every query sw_required over [0, first_q_token+1), which covers pending page 6 as one range, so with use_hw=true the predicate alone returns dense and only line 2556 makes the assertions at 3606-3611 pass. But that fixture is impossible in production: a page is pending only because it holds a token job with KV work (model.hpp:1922-1930), and every token job is a query in the forward's mask, where build_edge_ranges (ranged_mask.cpp:46-66) closes one range per query token. A pending page therefore spans one range only when its single new token sits at offset 63 (the decode step that fills the page); in prefill every pending page has per-token ranges and is non-dense for the kernel and the planner alike, with or without the term. (3) In that page-fill decode case under hardware attention the page's tokens are above the last DMA-complete shard, so the query is sw_required and the kernel's predicate yields an AMX visit; the planner would charge it 3 units instead of 1. The code gives no mechanism for the comment's "no AMX visit" claim, and the test pins the rule on a configuration that cannot occur. Impact on plan balance is small (at most one pending page per user per KV head, every 64th decode step), so the severity is low rather than medium, but the divergence from the kernel gate and the measurement-only justification are real.

confirmed.title: Test comment names the wrong reason for 'no query split'
confirmed.detail: Lines 3640-3641: 'One ready and one pending section per worker of the block; no query split (every worker already holds several page tasks).' In the pending pass every worker holds exactly one page task (p6 or p7), so the stated reason is false for that pass. The guard that actually prevents the split in both passes is split_sections_by_query's 'if (cands.empty() || page_tasks > n_workers / 2) continue;' (model.hpp:3067): page_tasks is 12 in the ready pass and 4 in the pending pass, both above n_workers / 2 = 2. Someone changing that guard would not learn from this comment that the n_sections == 4 assertion depends on it.
confirmed.fix: In /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-glimmer-planner/t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3640-3641 replace the parenthetical with the real guard, for example: "// One ready and one pending section per worker of the block. No query split: each pass has more page tasks (12 ready, 4 pending) than n_workers / 2 = 2, the page_tasks guard of split_sections_by_query, and the ready sections hold three pages each, so they are not split candidates."
confirmed.verdict: Verified in /home/jhan/workspace/ai-runs/tron-glimmer-planner. The test has 4 workers, 2 KV heads, 6 ready pages and 2 pending pages [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3475,3496-3497,3619]. The two-walk placement gives each worker one 3-page ready section and one 1-page pending section (the test itself asserts pending_workers == block, one per worker). So in the pending pass every worker holds exactly one page task, and the comment's reason "every worker already holds several page tasks" [t_llama_unit.cpp:3640-3641] is false for that pass. The split code does run here: cap = min(8 default, 4 workers) = 4 >= 2 and n_q = 64 >= split_min_queries 32 [model.hpp:137-140,3012-3014], and the pending sections are valid candidates (one page, scaled_vs 64, span 64). What stops the split in the pending pass is the total-count guard "page_tasks > n_workers / 2" [model.hpp:3067]: page_tasks = 12 (ready) and 4 (pending), both above 2. In the ready pass cands is also empty (3-page sections are not candidates). The n_sections == 2 * workers_per_kv_head assertion therefore depends on that guard, and the comment names a different, per-worker reason. This is a comment-contradicts-code defect, low severity, not a taste nit.

confirmed.title: The test's precondition (kill switch unset) is a comment, not a check
confirmed.detail: Line 3469-3470: 'The checks assume the default, TRON_PLAN_WEIGHTED_DISABLE unset.' plan_weighted_enabled() is read once per process from the environment, so with TRON_PLAN_WEIGHTED_DISABLE=1 in the test runner's environment the CHECKs at 3590-3604 fail with bare numbers (work() == 128 against 384) and nothing names the cause. tests.sh in exec/glimpl-20261017 runs t_amx_numerics a second time under TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1; a similar second run of this binary under the planner switch would produce exactly that misleading failure.
confirmed.verdict: Mechanism verified in the worktree. plan_weighted_enabled() [h/tron/models/common.hpp:705-711] reads TRON_PLAN_WEIGHTED_DISABLE once per process into a function-local static, and work() [common.hpp:729-735] returns scaled_vs when it is off. The test [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3471-3645] cannot set or reset the switch, and states its precondition only in a comment at 3469-3470. With TRON_PLAN_WEIGHTED_DISABLE=1 in the runner's environment: scaled_vs is 128 for every page (visits = 64 queries x 2 KV heads), so `partial_page.work() > dense_page.work()` [3590] fails as 128 > 128, `partial_page.work() == diagonal_cost` [3593] fails as 128 == 384 (3 x 126 + 3 x 2), `total.work() == ...` [3595] fails, and the one-walk placement puts both pending pages on the last worker of each head's block, so `pending_workers == block` [3637] and `n_sections == 4` [3640] fail too. Catch2 prints only the expression and the numbers; the cause (the switch) appears nowhere in the failure output. The same file already names host-dependent preconditions in the failure text (WARN at 2700, 2741), so an unnamed environment precondition is a gap against the file's own idiom, not a taste point. Two corrections to the finding's detail: (1) `dense_page.work() == amx_dense_visit_cost * visits` [3591] does NOT fail under the switch (128 == 128); the first bare-number failures are 3590 and 3593. rejected.title: Per-class share() rounding breaks the claimed exact invariance of split decisions for non-AMX models
rejected.reason: The finding's premise is false for the fixture it names. In check_page_range_reductions<65, true> (t/t_llama_unit.cpp:2745, instantiated at :3458 with window max and 32) the 65 queries sit at positions 63..127 and the two pages hold positions 0..63 and 64..127. A simulation of the mask (query j < 64 sees positions <= 63+j, inside the window; job 64 sees nothing) gives one visit class per page in every case: window max: page 0 = 64 full / 0 partial, page 1 = 0 full / 63 partial (position 127 is never visible, so no query sees all 64 tokens of page 1); window 32: page 0 = 0 full / 32 partial, page 1 = 0 full / 63 partial. Each page has exactly one nonzero class, so share(avx_full) + share(avx_partial) equals share(scaled_vs) exactly, every piece cost is exactly 3x the unit cost, and fixed_cost is 3 x 20 (model.hpp:3019-3021). All decisions in split_sections_by_query are ratios (load * inverse_speed comparisons, makespans[0] * (1 - min_gain), best_makespan * (1 + near_best); model.hpp:3100-3131), so a common factor of 3 leaves them unchanged. The fixture comment (t_llama_unit.cpp:3094-3096) is therefore correct, and the model.hpp comment the finding cites (3017-3021) describes the units of fixed_cost and makes no invariance claim. The new test case at t_llama_unit.cpp:3471+ only checks estimate_work classification and never calls split_sections_by_query. For production non-AMX models with genuinely mixed pages the per-class floor can differ from the single-class floor by at most 1 visit per class per piece, i.e. at most 3 cost units out of a piece cost of at least 3 x (32 + 20) = 156, under 2 % of an estimate that is already approximate (every visit of a class is charged the same regardless of k_tokens); that is not a defect and no assertion depends on it. The proposed fix (derive avx_partial as vs - amx - full) would change nothing in the fixture and is a taste choice elsewhere.

rejected.title: EAGLE comment claims 'never dense'; the kernel keeps offset 0 for the q_position 0 query
rejected.reason: The finding's premise does not hold. For the query at position 0 the kernel does keep begin = 0 [self_attention.hpp:1869], but the page still cannot pass is_dense_amx_page: that predicate also requires `pg.at_offset(page_size - 1) < range.tok_hi` [self_attention.hpp:215-216], and the query at position 0 is the root token of the tree mask, so the only range visible to it is the one holding kv token 0 (tok_hi = 1; a 64-token page's last token is never below it). The kernel therefore runs the dotter (AVX) for that visit with one relevant k token, and the planner also counts it as AVX partial (first_offset = 1 makes the dense test fail, while k_tokens still counts token 0 because run.begin is not shifted) [model.hpp:2565, 2610-2616]. Planner and kernel agree on the path; the comment's operative claim "is never dense" is correct. The only imprecision is the clause "never starts at offset 0", which is literally false for the q_position 0 query but has no effect on the estimate; that is a wording nit, not a comment-contradicts-code defect.

rejected.title: work_estimate_t can now carry scaled_vs without any visit, and nothing checks the invariant
rejected.reason: The fixture inconsistency is real but has no observable effect, so this is a consistency note, not a defect. Facts checked in the worktree: (1) t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:835 builds {.scaled_vs = 1} with no visit counters, so work() is 0 under the default weights and 1 with TRON_PLAN_WEIGHTED_DISABLE=1 (common.hpp:731-734). The commit did not touch this file. (2) Nothing in that test reads work(): assign_page on an empty worker plan creates a new section regardless of work() (common.hpp:988-990 only compares against an existing back section); the test then sets software_plan.work_estimate = {1.0f} by hand (line 836), so the model.hpp:2443 sum is bypassed; the execution path (self_attention.hpp:1196, :1518) passes section.work_estimate only into a perfetto trace argument (scaled_vs, k_dot_products, kv_heads) and never calls work(). No zero-work skip exists in execution: the only 'work() == 0' test is the planner's section_cost at model.hpp:3026. So the test's behaviour is identical under both switch states. (3) The invariant already has a test owner in the commit: t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3580-3588 checks scaled_vs == visits and that amx_dense + avx_full + avx_partial partition those visits for every page in both pending states, with AMX on and off. (4) The proposed debug assert in work_estimate_t would be wrong: split_sections_by_query (model.hpp:3090-3095) shares each field with per-field floor division, and floor of a sum is not the sum of floors, so a piece's scaled_vs can legitimately differ from the sum of its three visit counters. An assert placed only at the end of estimate_work would hold but duplicates the unit test. Under the review rules (concrete defects only, no taste nits) this does not qualify.

rejected.title: std::initializer_list used by name without its header
rejected.reason: The fact is right: model.hpp:2930 names std::initializer_list and the include block has no <initializer_list>. The consequence claimed ("a header reshuffle in libstdc++ or a switch to -fmodules would break the build") is wrong. The C++ standard header synopses for <vector> ([vector.syn]), <array> ([array.syn]) and <algorithm> ([algorithm.syn]) each contain the line `#include <initializer_list>`, so any conforming library guarantees the name after the includes model.hpp already has at lines 5, 6 and 25. A modules build (`import std;`) exports std::initializer_list as well. So there is no build configuration in which this line fails. What remains is include-what-you-use hygiene, and the codebase does not apply that consistently: h/common/mask.hpp (lines 272, 494, 716) and h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:49 name std::initializer_list without the header, while ten other files include it. Neither the C++ guide nor the Wade checklist has an include-what-you-use rule (Wade check 14 is the opposite: an added include needs a consumer). This is a taste nit, not a defect.
